metadata.title: WELL-BEING QUESTIONNAIRE FOR PISA 2022 (International Option) Main Survey Version

survey_design.weight_fields_interpretation: This document is a questionnaire instrument specification for PISA 2022 well-being items, not an empirical analysis of student achievement or a predictive modeling study. As such, it does not provide sampling frames, replicate-weight schemes, or any weight variable names (e.g., W_FSTUWT, TOTWGT) to apply in estimation. For any downstream empirical use of these items, analysts should use the official PISA sampling weights and replicate weights provided with the PISA microdata for the relevant cycle and country, and apply them according to the PISA technical documentation to obtain population-representative estimates and correct standard errors under the complex survey design. No guidance on weighting is included here because the file only defines item wording, response options, and routing filters.

data.handling_not_reported_explanation: Plausible Values (PVs) are generated for cognitive achievement domains in PISA, but this document only specifies well-being questionnaire items (e.g., health, satisfaction, relationships, feelings) and does not report any PV-based outcome or scaling model. Missing-data handling is also not described because the file is an instrument/version specification rather than an analysis paper; it does not present an analytic dataset, estimation procedure, or imputation/deletion rules. Therefore, both PV handling and missing-data handling are not applicable/not reported in the context of this questionnaire documentation.

sample_details.sample_filtering_criteria: Not applicable: this is a questionnaire instrument specification (item codes, response categories, and filter routing) and does not define an analytic subsample from PISA microdata.

data.outcome_summary: This document provides the PISA 2022 well-being questionnaire (International Option) main survey version, specifying item identifiers (e.g., WB150–WB178), question wording, response formats (single-select, numeric entry, and multi-row Likert-style items), and filter routing (e.g., students who report never attending a class are routed to later items). It does not include any study design, sampling strategy, or analytic results, and it does not define a dependent variable for predictive modeling. Because no empirical estimation is performed, there are no reported performance metrics, benchmarks, or model comparisons. The key contribution is measurement specification: it enables consistent construction of well-being indicators across participating countries and provides the structure needed for later psychometric scaling and survey analysis in the PISA framework. Any policy interpretation would depend on subsequent empirical analyses using these items, which are not included here.
data.null_fields_interpretation: This extraction is sparse because the provided text is an instrument/questionnaire specification rather than an empirical research article. There is no reported sample size, country coverage, weighting approach, PV/scaling method, missing-data strategy, or ML modeling/evaluation. Consequently, fields related to empirical findings and ML techniques are intentionally left empty, and the questionnaire items are not treated as model predictors/outcomes within this document.
